lead: The overnight batch keeps a reported AI-attributed eviction, competing sabotage claims and a lithography policy argument at their evidence level. An in-browser inference experiment and a plugin-design probe carry single-author measurement limits.

sections.title: An automated assurance is not yet an adjudicated obligation
sections.intro: A reported eviction after AI-attributed rent emails raises disclosure and liability questions that remain factually and legally open.

sections.title: Sabotage allegations and a vendor denial both remain unverified
sections.intro: New social posts claim intentional interference while an Anthropic-affiliated response denies it; neither side's evidence was inspectable here.

sections.title: In-browser inference trades prompt speed for locality
sections.intro: An experimental WebAssembly engine approaches native generation speed on one machine while lagging badly on prompt processing.

sections.title: A model as API design probe
sections.intro: datasette-charts improved its plugin hook after a Claude-built prototype exposed friction points.

sections.title: Prediction tracking needs its own methodology check
sections.intro: A visible match example is not an accuracy rate, and the site's scoring was not reviewed.

sections.title: Export controls can strand the technology they guard
sections.intro: A lithography veteran argues the MATCH Act could hand serviced, reverse-engineerable scanners to rivals.
